etymology: From law: a plea that asks the court to apply a different rule to this case, with no reason given for the exception.
committed_when: A rule the speaker has just applied to someone else would now apply to the speaker.
tell: The rule holds, except here, for reasons that are never stated as a rule.
counter: Ask what makes this case different in a way that could be written down and applied to everyone.
senses: Applying a standard to others while exempting oneself, without giving a reason that would not also exempt the others.
It works because the exemption is usually framed as context. Every rule has context; the fallacy is invoking it only for one side.
example: “Attacking a public official's family is out of bounds.” Said by the account that spent last spring on a mayor's brother.

confused_with.tell: Special pleading asks for an exemption from the standard; two wrongs argues the standard is void because someone else broke it.
